plan:
CYCLENET FOR PERIODIC TIME SERIES — FINAL EXPERIMENT DESIGN (paper design; no experiment run or claimed)

SCOPE STATUS: Design-only. CONFIRMED workspace facts: /workspace contains only task.json; embedded track.md states "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required"; Python 3.14.4 system environment with no ML packages installed; network disabled; no GPU. Everything below beyond these facts is a design assumption or a stated default, labeled as such.

=====================================================================
1. HYPOTHESIS
=====================================================================
Primary hypothesis: adding a Residual Cycle Forecasting (RCF) component — a cycle-indexed learnable periodic matrix — to a lightweight residual backbone improves multi-step forecasting accuracy on series with periodic patterns, relative to the same backbone without RCF, with the improvement growing with (a) the strength of the periodic component and (b) longer forecast horizons.

=====================================================================
2. MODEL: CYCLENET COMPONENTS TO BE SPECIFIED
=====================================================================
All components are design specifications (assumed architecture follows the published CycleNet/RCF description; no reference implementation exists in the workspace — assumption flagged).

2.1 Residual Cycle Forecasting (RCF) module
- Learnable parameter matrix W_c ∈ R^{cycleLen × d} (cycleLen = period length in time steps; d = number of channels/series).
- At training and inference, for each sample with lookback window covering timestamps t₀ … t₀+L−1 and forecast horizon t₀+L … t₀+L+H−1:
  - Input augmentation: x_input = x_raw + W_c[(t mod cycleLen) indices of the lookback window]
  - Output correction: ŷ = y_backbone(x_input) − W_c[(t mod cycleLen) indices of the horizon window]
  i.e., the periodic component is added back for the forecast region; the backbone only models the residual (trend/noise/irregular part).
- W_c is trained jointly with the backbone by backprop (it is a plain parameter tensor — gradient flows through both the input-add and output-subtract paths).
- Initialization: zeros (so at step 0 the model reduces to the plain backbone; the periodic structure is learned). Rationale: avoids a random-periodicity prior corrupting early training; assumption, stated as a default.

2.2 Normalization wrapper (RevIN-style instancenorm)
- Per-window: subtract the lookback-window mean, divide by its std (per channel), run backbone+RCF, then de-normalize the output (add mean, multiply std). Applied around the whole model. Mitigates level shifts; standard practice; assumed default.

2.3 Residual backbone (two variants)
- B1 "Linear": single learnable linear map from flattened L·d input to H·d output (per-channel shared or channel-independent; default: channel-independent linear, matching DLinear-style simplicity).
- B2 "MLP": L·d → hidden (256) → H·d, one hidden layer, ReLU. Rationale for keeping both: tests whether RCF's benefit is orthogonal to backbone capacity.

=====================================================================
3. RESOLVED DESIGN CHOICE (1): PERIOD / CYCLE-LENGTH SELECTION
=====================================================================
Primary strategy:
- Synthetic data (primary protocol): cycleLen is KNOWN a priori by construction (it is a generation parameter) and supplied to the model. This removes period-estimation error from the primary comparison, isolating the RCF mechanism.
- Real-data extension (optional, clearly labeled): cycleLen estimated from data by FFT periodogram + ACF confirmation on the training split only (no test leakage). Primary estimator: dominant FFT peak over the training series after detrending, validated by checking ACF local maximum at the candidate lag; ties broken toward the shorter candidate consistent with domain priors (e.g., 24 for hourly data). This is a stated default procedure, not an executed result.

Fallback behavior under mis-specified periods:
- Robustness experiment (in-scope, synthetic): inject the model with a deliberately wrong cycleLen (true period p, supplied period p' ∈ {p/2, 2p, p±1}) and measure degradation. Expected (hypothesis-supporting) pattern: graceful degradation when p' is an integer multiple/divisor of p (RCF can still express the true period) and larger degradation when p' is an incompatible near-neighbor (p±1).
- If period estimation is uncertain on real data, the design prescribes selecting cycleLen on the validation split by grid over ACF/FFT candidates (validation-set model selection — no test-set tuning), with the fallback default cycleLen = 24 for hourly / 7·24 for daily-aggregated data when no dominant peak is found (assumed defaults).

=====================================================================
4. RESOLVED DESIGN CHOICE (2): DATASET SCOPE
=====================================================================
PRIMARY — synthetic protocol (no external data needed, consistent with confirmed "repositories not required"):
- Generator: y_t = trend_t + A·sin(2π t / p + φ) + optional secondary harmonic + AR(1) or iid noise + optional level shift mid-series.
- Grid over factors: period p ∈ {24, 48, 168}; amplitude-to-noise ratio SNR ∈ {0.5, 2, 10} (low/medium/high periodicity); trend strength ∈ {none, linear}; n_channels d ∈ {1, 7}; series length 10,000 steps (≈ 5,600/800/3,600 train/val/test at 70/10/20, period-boundary-aligned). Full grid = 3×3×2×2 = 36 configurations; each run is cheap (Section 9).
- Seeds: 3 generation seeds × 3 training seeds per configuration (generation seed controls phase φ and noise realization; training seed controls init/order).

OPTIONAL EXTENSION (clearly labeled; described but not required and not executed): one public hourly dataset (electricity or traffic, standard long-horizon TSF benchmarks) with 70/10/20 chronological split, H ∈ {24, 48, 96}, cycleLen from Section 3 estimator. This requires data the workspace does not have; it is included as a design addendum only.

=====================================================================
5. RESOLVED DESIGN CHOICE (3): HYPERPARAMETER DEFAULTS (stated defaults with rationale)
=====================================================================
- Lookback L = 2·cycleLen (e.g., L=48 for p=24). Rationale: two full periods give the RCF index enough coverage of all cycle positions while keeping the backbone input small; ablation over L ∈ {1·p, 2·p, 4·p} is included.
- Horizon H = 96 (4 periods for p=24), with per-horizon reporting at H ∈ {24, 48, 96}. Rationale: standard long-horizon TSF convention; multiple horizons let us test the "benefit grows with horizon" prediction.
- Model sizes: Linear backbone L·d → H·d (per channel); MLP hidden width 256. Parameter counts are small (<0.5M) by design — the claim under test is that periodicity handling, not capacity, drives improvement.
- Training: Adam, lr = 1e-3 (Linear) / 5e-4 (MLP), cosine decay to 1e-5, batch size 64 (sliding windows), max 20 epochs with early stopping on validation MSE (patience 5). Loss: MSE (matches primary metric). These are conventional defaults; a small lr sweep {1e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2} is prescribed on one synthetic config only, to bound tuning cost.
- All hyperparameters fixed across model variants so comparisons are apples-to-apples; validation split used for early stopping only.

=====================================================================
6. CONTROLS AND COMPARISONS (distinct sections, per researcher instruction)
=====================================================================
6.1 Baseline comparisons (external references — different methods, same data/protocol):
  A. Backbone-only (Linear, no RCF) — the critical comparison; identical backbone isolates the cycle module.
  B. Backbone-only MLP.
  C. Seasonal-Naive: ŷ_{t+h} = x_{t+h−k·p} (repeat last observed period); strong periodic-data baseline.
  D. Periodic-mean baseline: per-(position-in-cycle) training-split mean, extended over the horizon.
  E. (Optional extension only) published numbers / standard implementations on the real benchmark.
6.2 Ablations (internal to CycleNet — same architecture, one factor changed):
  A1. RCF removed (≡ baseline A; included in both lists for completeness).
  A2. RCF present but with cycle index randomly shuffled per batch (destroys the period↔position alignment while preserving parameter count) — tests that the benefit comes from correct cycle indexing, not extra parameters.
  A3. Correct cycleLen vs. mis-specified cycleLen (Section 3 fallback study).
  A4. Lookback length L ∈ {1p, 2p, 4p} with RCF fixed.
  A5. Normalization wrapper on/off.
6.3 Controls on the data protocol itself: SNR=0.5 (near-dominant noise) configurations serve as an "adversarial" control where RCF should help little or not at all; a pure-noise (no periodicity) control configuration verifies RCF does not hallucinate periodic structure when none exists (performance should match baseline A within noise).

=====================================================================
7. ANALYSIS PLAN
=====================================================================
Primary metric: MSE on the test split; secondary: MAE. Reported per horizon and averaged, mean ± std over 3 training seeds; generation seeds pooled or reported separately (decision: report both; per-generation-seed pairing is used for significance testing).
Statistical testing: paired comparison across the 9 (3 gen × 3 train) seeds per configuration; Wilcoxon signed-rank or paired t-test (whichever is appropriate after checking seed-pair differences), α = 0.05, with Holm correction across the 3 horizons.

Result patterns SUPPORTING the hypothesis:
  (i) A (backbone+RCF) beats A1 (backbone alone) on MSE at all horizons on medium/high-SNR configs, with the gap widening in H and in SNR — the dose–response signature.
  (ii) A beats A2 (shuffled index) by a margin similar to the A vs. A1 gap — confirming the cycle alignment is the active ingredient.
  (iii) On the no-periodicity control, A ≈ A1 (no spurious harm) — specificity.
  (iv) A3 fallback pattern: mild degradation at p' ∈ {p/2, 2p}, larger at p' = p±1 — consistent with the RCF mechanism.

Patterns REFUTING / weakening the hypothesis:
  (i') A ≈ A1 across all SNRs and horizons (RCF adds nothing beyond what L=2p lookback already provides).
  (ii') A2 ≈ A (benefit is from extra parameters, not alignment).
  (iii') A < A1 only at low SNR or shows instability across seeds (high variance) — benefit not robust.
  (iv') Mis-specified periods cause catastrophic failure rather than graceful degradation — fragility undermines the method's practical value.
Decision rule: the hypothesis is supported only if (i) holds with Holm-corrected significance at H=96 on ≥2 of 3 SNR levels AND (ii) holds directionally; otherwise the design treats RCF's benefit as unestablished.

=====================================================================
8. IMPLEMENTATION PLAN (to be written, not executed)
=====================================================================
Deliverables: (a) single-file NumPy/PyTorch-CPU implementation of RCF + backbones + generator + evaluation loop; (b) config file enumerating the 36-configuration grid + ablations; (c) results schema (per-run JSON: config, seed, horizon, MSE/MAE, parameter count, wallclock); (d) aggregation/plotting script (per-horizon MSE vs. SNR curves, ablation tables).
Code structure: `rcf.py` (module), `backbones.py`, `data.py` (generator + windowing + splits), `train.py`, `evaluate.py`, `aggregate.py`. Windowing must compute cycle indices from absolute timestamps so phase is consistent across train/test windows (a common subtle bug the design explicitly guards against; a unit check is prescribed: RCF output on a noise-free pure sinusoid should equal the sinusoid up to backbone error).

=====================================================================
9. FEASIBILITY STATEMENT (consistent with confirmed environment)
=====================================================================
- Confirmed: CPU-only, 224 cores, no GPU, no preinstalled packages; network disabled. Therefore the design mandates dependency installation as an explicit setup step (torch CPU, numpy, pandas — assumption: permitted install; if not, a pure-NumPy fallback implementation of the Linear backbone + RCF is specified, which is fully feasible since RCF is a learnable matrix trained by least squares/gradient descent and the Linear backbone is a single affine map trainable with closed-form ridge or simple SGD).
- Scale estimate (design estimate, not a measurement): per synthetic run — ~7,000 training windows, model <0.5M params, 20 epochs max; a NumPy implementation should train in <1–2 minutes per run; a PyTorch-CPU run in <30 s per epoch worst case, so minutes per run. Full grid (36 configs × 3 gen × 3 train seeds × ~4 model variants incl. ablations ≈ 1,300 runs) at ~2 min each ≈ 43 CPU-hours, trivially parallelizable across 224 cores → well under 1 hour wallclock with process-level parallelism. Memory per run is dominated by the window tensor (≈ 7,000 × 48 floats ≈ a few MB) — negligible.
- Optional public-benchmark extension would need external data acquisition and is therefore explicitly out of the guaranteed scope given the confirmed network-disabled environment; it is feasible only if data files are supplied.
- Everything above is a feasibility estimate based on standard complexity reasoning; no run has been performed and no runtime has been measured.

=====================================================================
10. CONFIRMED vs. ASSUMED — SUMMARY TABLE
=====================================================================
CONFIRMED (from workspace inspection):
  • Design-only scope; repositories and compute not required (track.md in task.json).
  • No datasets, code, or CycleNet references in /workspace.
  • CPU-only (224 cores), no GPU, network disabled, Python 3.14.4, no ML packages installed.

ASSUMED / STATED DEFAULTS (require no further confirmation for a paper design, but are not workspace facts):
  • CycleNet architecture follows the published RCF description (learnable cycleLen×d matrix, add-at-input/subtract-at-output, joint training).
  • Hyperparameter defaults in Section 5 (L=2p, H=96, lr, epochs, batch size).
  • Synthetic generator parameterization in Section 4; public benchmark as optional extension.
  • Period-selection procedure and mis-specification behavior (Section 3).
  • Runtime estimates in Section 9 are analytical, not measured.

This design makes no claim that any experiment, training run, or measurement has been performed.

1. HYPOTHESIS
=====================================================================
Primary hypothesis: adding a Residual Cycle Forecasting (RCF) component — a cycle-indexed learnable periodic matrix — to a lightweight residual backbone improves multi-step forecasting accuracy on series with periodic patterns, relative to the same backbone without RCF, with the improvement growing with (a) the strength of the periodic component and (b) longer forecast horizons.

=====================================================================

=====================================================================
All components are design specifications (assumed architecture follows the published CycleNet/RCF description; no reference implementation exists in the workspace — assumption flagged).

2.1 Residual Cycle Forecasting (RCF) module
- Learnable parameter matrix W_c ∈ R^{cycleLen × d} (cycleLen = period length in time steps; d = number of channels/series).
- At training and inference, for each sample with lookback window covering timestamps t₀ … t₀+L−1 and forecast horizon t₀+L … t₀+L+H−1:
  - Input augmentation: x_input = x_raw + W_c[(t mod cycleLen) indices of the lookback window]
  - Output correction: ŷ = y_backbone(x_input) − W_c[(t mod cycleLen) indices of the horizon window]
  i.e., the periodic component is added back for the forecast region; the backbone only models the residual (trend/noise/irregular part).
- W_c is trained jointly with the backbone by backprop (it is a plain parameter tensor — gradient flows through both the input-add and output-subtract paths).
- Initialization: zeros (so at step 0 the model reduces to the plain backbone; the periodic structure is learned). Rationale: avoids a random-periodicity prior corrupting early training; assumption, stated as a default.

2.2 Normalization wrapper (RevIN-style instancenorm)
- Per-window: subtract the lookback-window mean, divide by its std (per channel), run backbone+RCF, then de-normalize the output (add mean, multiply std). Applied around the whole model. Mitigates level shifts; standard practice; assumed default.

2.3 Residual backbone (two variants)
- B1 "Linear": single learnable linear map from flattened L·d input to H·d output (per-channel shared or channel-independent; default: channel-independent linear, matching DLinear-style simplicity).
